   [I cannot use my card] and [the reason is that it is not working]

   (a) It is not true that I cannot use my card (so I can use it) OR

 If we simply change the main clause to positive, we get:
   "I can use my card because it is not working." 
 But that doesn't make sense because if it's not working, then we wouldn't be able to use it.

 What we really want to negate is the entire causal statement?

   The speaker is saying that the card is broken and that's why they cannot use it.
